issues.failure_explanation: N_P counts literally equal branches, whereas equivalence permits branches to be replaced by different equivalent representatives. Let A=[[]_0 []_1]_0 and B=[[]_1 []_0]_0. Then A and B are distinct but equivalent, with S(A)=S(B)=1. Consequently [A A]_0 and [A B]_0 are equivalent, but their symmetry orders are respectively 2 and 1. Thus S is not well-defined on ULN-trees.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define N_P using equivalence of branches rather than literal equality, and verify invariance by the same recursive induction.
issues.overall_effect: The representative-independent definition of ULN symmetry order and the expansion containing that quantity fail at higher orders. The elementary-coefficient vanishing conditions themselves do not require this invariance.
issues.title: Symmetry order is not invariant under tree equivalence
issues.why_classification: This is a local repair of the symmetry definition; it requires no new numerical method, order conditions, or convergence-rate loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\rhof{\cdot}$ is a seminorm on the vector space $\R^{p} \times \R^{p\times q}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof replaces a squared seminorm of a martingale difference by the difference of two expected squared seminorms. This is a Hilbert-space variance identity, not a property of arbitrary seminorms. For the l1 norm on R², let X be (1,0) or (0,1) with equal probabilities and condition on the trivial sigma-field. Then Eρ²(X)-ρ²(EX)=0, whereas Eρ²(X-EX)=1. The required comparison therefore fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict ρ to a quadratic seminorm, ρ(v)^2=v^TQv with Q positive semidefinite, and carry out the conditional-variance estimates in that seminorm.
issues.overall_effect: The general-seminorm stability and convergence arguments are unsupported. This root does not defeat the Euclidean and Y-projection cases of the corollary, where conditional orthogonality is available.
issues.title: Conditional variance identities are used for arbitrary seminorms
issues.why_classification: A substantive structural restriction on the allowed seminorms is needed, but it preserves both concrete seminorm choices and avoids replacing the global stability architecture.
